extracted.intended_audience: U.S. policymakers, patent stakeholders, patent practitioners, and interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and provisions discussed in Senate debate on S.23 (the America Invents Act) about improving patent quality, USPTO operations, and procedures for examination, challenges, and small-entity access. The rubric items are the bill features and policy goals used to evaluate or design patent-system reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen patent quality and result in more fairness for both patent holders and patent challengers; ensure patents issued are of good quality and will provide good defense against future challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General bill goal repeated throughout debate: reforms are intended to 'improve patent quality,' 'strengthen patent quality,' and 'help create good jobs, encourage innovation.' The Record connects higher quality to increased outside participation, improved examination processes, and more rigorous post-issuance review mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition to first-to-file system
rubrics_metrics.description: Move the United States to a first-to-file system: 'By moving the United States to a first-to-file system, the bill simplifies the process of acquiring rights.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated benefits: 'reduce legal costs, improve fairness, and support U.S. innovators seeking to market their products and services in a global marketplace.' The bill also preserves protections: 'an inventor’s patent priority is protected for a year if he or she is the first to publicly disclose an invention.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, objective guidelines and predictability
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO must have clear, objective guidelines that enable an applicant to predict whether his or her application will be approved; improve the predictability and accuracy of the patent examination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debate emphasizes need for objective standards so applicants can 'predict' outcomes and for PTO to move away from reliance on secret files; 'PTO’s task of determining the priority of a patent application will be more straightforward because patent priority will depend on objective, public facts.'

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO fee-setting authority (self-adjusting fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the USPTO authority to establish and adjust its fees to reflect changes in costs, demand, and workload; ensure full cost recovery at no taxpayer expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: give PTO 'tools it needs to address the unacceptably long backlog' and enhance productivity--reducing delay. Statement: 'By providing authority for the USPTO to establish and adjust its fees ... the bill would enhance productivity--reducing delay in the patent application process--and ensure full cost recovery at no taxpayer expense.'

rubrics_metrics.name: End patent fee diversion / protect user-fee funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent diversion of patent fees from PTO to the Treasury; ensure patent fees are available to PTO for planning and staffing instead of being treated as a general revenue source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes more than $800 million diverted in past 20 years; fee diversion 'cripples the ability of PTO to do its job' and robs PTO of ability to plan. Support for amendments to ensure PTO has access to fees, subject to congressional oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce backlog and improve timeliness of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce delays such as the current multi-year waits for first action and issuance (noted as ~2 years to first action, ~3+ years to final issues); process applications expeditiously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics cited: backlog numbers (700,000 awaiting first action; 500,000 in process; 1.2 million pending), 'it takes two years for an inventor to get an initial ruling' and 'another year or more' for issuance. Proposed responses include fee-setting, hiring more examiners, prioritized examination, and administrative reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination / Three-Track (fast lane) with small-entity fee considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide mechanisms for prioritized examination (a 'fast lane') including options for applicants to pay a higher fee to guarantee an application ruling within a year; consider reduced fees for small entities requesting prioritized examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debate references a 'higher fee to guarantee that their applications will receive a ruling within a year' and amendments (e.g., Bennet amendment) to 'reduce the fee amounts paid by small entities requesting prioritized examination under Three-Track Examination.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow third-party pre-issuance submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit third parties to provide submissions regarding prior art before a patent is issued to assist examiners in assessing novelty/obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a tool to 'leverage the knowledge of outside parties' and 'enhancing the ability of examiners to determine whether an application is for a truly innovative idea worthy of the protection of a patent.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review: 9-month window allowing challenges on any grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a 9-month post-grant review process during which third parties can challenge a patent on any grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combined with pre-issuance submissions, the post-grant review is presented as producing 'a more rigorous and more thorough vetting of patent applications' and resulting in 'stronger, higher quality patents.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination process for business-method patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a process for reexamination of business-method patents by the Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senate managers’ amendment incorporates Senator Schumer's suggestion to provide a process for reexamination of business method patents; presented as a measure to 'improve patent quality.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Patent Ombudsman Program for small businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorize the Director to establish a Patent Ombudsman Program whose staff duties include 'providing support and services relating to patent filings to small business concerns.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: a 'fast lane' and assistance to help small businesses navigate patent filing bureaucracy; part of efforts to help small entities obtain patents and foster innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create USPTO satellite offices to broaden operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Open USPTO satellite offices (example: Detroit) to tap regional patent practitioner communities, universities, and diverse workforces while reducing costs and improving operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director Kappos chose Detroit because it 'had large communities of patent lawyers and agents, nearby universities and transportation centers, and relatively low costs of living and real estate.' Satellite offices are part of administrative reforms to 'enhance operations of the Patent and Trademark Office.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase examiner staffing and revise performance evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Add substantial numbers of examiners (goal: more than 1,000 examiners per year for two years; 30 percent increase noted) and update examiner performance evaluation measures to improve productivity and reduce attrition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debate notes PTO hiring freezes and calls for staffing increases; Kappos reported productivity gains and collaboration with examiner union to revise yardsticks for performance evaluation ('the first time in 50 years that the yardsticks had been revised').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use user-fee funding for PTO operations (self-funded model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize PTO as a user-fee supported organization that should be allowed to pass through staffing and operational costs to applicants rather than relying on appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: PTO 'is a user-fee supported organization and so it should be able to pass through the costs of staffing needs to patent applicants.' This ties to fee-setting authority and ending fee diversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extraneous or counterproductive provisions (venue/damages caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude or remove provisions (e.g., certain damages and venue rules) that may be unnecessary or risk stunting development of case law; evaluate whether recent court decisions make such provisions redundant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration 'would not object to removal of these provisions' and Senators argued removing certain damages and venue provisions that are 'no longer needed' in light of court decisions. One Senator warned that current venue language 'risks stunting the development of case law.'
